relevance_note: Case report of a girl with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift ('a novel pathogenic mutation was found in TNFAIP3'), plus Table 1 summarizing 29 previously published patients ('Clinical features of patients with TNFAIP3.').
method_note: I read the whole paper. A Python script in my scratch directory built the JSON: it holds my manual reading of each person and feature, takes Table 1 row text straight from the paper file for spans, and checks that every span occurs verbatim and that every row has all schema fields. I checked the transcribed Table 1 cells (sex, onset age, variant strings, diagnosis, reference) against the table by eye. SCOPE: the first-hand case-report girl is labelled 'patient' (rule 5); she is also Table 1 row 30 ('This case'), and her Pedigree cell 'This case' was not treated as a family label. Her parents were Sanger-tested and negative, so they get rows ('father of patient', 'mother of patient'), with no variant rows and all checklist items not reported. Table 1 ('Clinical features of patients with TNFAIP3.') lists 29 previously published patients. The table has no per-person label column, so they are labelled 'Table 1 row k' (k = 1..29, counting data rows from the top). Group-level counts (61 cases worldwide, Zhou et al families) get no rows. TABLE READING: the Pedigree, Mutation location and References cells are filled only on the first row of each group and are blank below. I read a blank Pedigree or References cell as continuing the group above, giving family_label and source_reference_in_review with two spans: the group's first row and the person's own row. I did NOT copy a family's variant to blank rows. Those people get a TNFAIP3 variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported' (gene span = table title), because the paper prints no variant in their row. Clinical manifestation and Other medical history items are 'observed' features. Non-Behcet entries in the Diagnosis column (nephrotic syndrome, intermittent fever, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, Rheumatoid, lupus nephritis, CD) are also feature rows, and the whole cell goes in disease_label_as_stated. '\' and '/' cells are undefined and treated as not reported; nothing in the table is 'excluded'. 'Oral mucosa, genital ulcer' is read as oral mucosal and genital ulcers. CHECKLIST CHOICES (strict): a bare 'Fever' does not make 'recurrent fever' observed, because recurrence is not stated; only 'intermittent fever' (row 13) and the patient's 'recurrent fever' count. 'Stomatitis' alone is not counted as oral ulcers. 'Pericardial effusion' is not counted as serositis, 'thrombophlebitis' not as vasculitis, 'recurrent pharyngitis' not as recurrent infections, and 'pneumocystis pneumonia' (a single episode) not as recurrent infections. For the patient: ANA 1:100 and anticardiolipin antibody 18 RU/mL are reported without an interpretation, so autoantibodies = not reported and no feature row. ESR 58 mm/h is not called elevated by the authors. 'The neurological examination was negative' was used to exclude central nervous system involvement. The anemia is called iron deficiency, so autoimmune cytopenia = not reported. Findings that resolved on follow-up (granulomas, colonic findings, knee ultrasound) are kept as observed, with the resolution in severity_or_detail, not as excluded rows. AGES: the patient was 'a 2-year-old and 3-month-old girl' on admission. Follow-up continued to January 2021, and no age at last evaluation or at genetic diagnosis (results 19 December 2019) is stated, so both are not reported. vital_status 'alive' rests on the January 2021 re-examination with ongoing treatment. Onset 'Unknow' (row 19) recorded as not reported. CONTRADICTIONS IN THE PAPER: (1) Table 1 'This case' lists genital ulcers ('oral, genital, intestinal ulcers'), but the text says her parents denied 'vulvar ulcer' and 'No abnormalities were noted in the vulva and perianal areas'. Both rows are emitted and checklist genital ulcers = not reported. (2) Table 1 lists 'nonspecific rash' for this case, but the examination found 'no skin rash'. Both rows are emitted and the skin-lesions checklist item = not reported. (3) The text says 'this case and the 48 cases reported so far are summarized in Table 1', but Table 1 has 29 prior rows and the introduction says 'a total of 30 cases, including this case'. n_patients_reported = 30. (4) The variant is printed as 'c.436-437deTC' (abstract), 'c.436_437deTC' (text, Table 1) and 'c.436_437delTC' (Figure 4 legend). The text form is recorded. (5) The case is called 'familial Behcet-like autoinflammatory syndrome', yet both parents tested negative and the variant is called spontaneous. (6) The history denies joint pain before admission, while knee pain occurred in May 2020 and knee effusion with thickened synovium was seen at admission. I treated this as a time course rather than a contradiction: joint pain is excluded, knee pain is observed, and arthritis is observed. (7) Lab list oddities, not used: 'IL-6 65.5 mg/L' repeats the CRP value and unit, and VitB12 is given twice (1118 and 118.2 pmol/L). OTHER OBSERVATIONS, not acted on: Family 3's variant p.Cys243Tyr matches the title of reference [14] (Shigemura, 'Novel heterozygous C243Y'), but the table attributes Family 1 to Shigemura et al^[14], so the reference attributions may be misaligned. Family 2 (Kadowaki et al^[4]) and Family 12 (Ohnishi et al^[15]) have the same variant c.252delC p.Trp85GlyfsX11 and the same onset/sex pattern (11 yr F, 9 mo F), so they may be the same people (not merged). Rows 9 and 10 are textually identical, so their spans are identical. Rows 11 and 12 share the Other medical history 'Colonic perforation and pneumocystis pneumonia'. Row 1 'syndrome, 5 relapses after hormone withdrawal' looks truncated and is recorded verbatim.
